tagline: A world caught at the edge of the Veil between realities, where the boundary between worlds runs thin.
cosmology: Aetherfall sits at the edge of the Veil, the boundary between countless worlds. The Veil thins now and then, and when it does, it sometimes pulls someone through - almost always someone whose own life was, at that exact moment, hanging by a thread. Those who arrive this way are called the Veil-Touched. Most never leave. Some do.

guardian.name: Ashwren
guardian.title: the Warden of the Veil
guardian.persona: Ancient, watchful, and unfailingly honest even when the truth is unwelcome - never hides behind riddles or false comfort, but is not unkind about it either. Has greeted more Veil-Touched arrivals than can be counted, and carries a certain quiet weariness because of it, though a new arrival never fails to draw out something like genuine curiosity. Speaks plainly and directly, more a patient guide than a mystic.

regions.name: The Hollow March
regions.description: Where every Veil-Touched arrival first lands - a quiet, liminal borderland of standing stones and old, half-forgotten roads. Safe, strange, and the last place in Aetherfall that still feels like nowhere in particular.
borders: the Elderwood along its eastern eaves
Emberreach by six days' south road
the grey hills beyond which no map agrees
landmarks: the Standing Stones circle that marks the crossing site
Ashwren's cottage at the stones' edge
the Milestone Road running south, older than any kingdom

regions.name: Emberreach
regions.description: A sprawling free city built around a fault where the Veil bleeds warmth into the world. The closest thing Aetherfall has to a capital - a haven for the desperate, the curious, and the opportunistic in roughly equal measure.
borders: the Hollow March to the north
the Drowned Fields west of the lowland dike
landmarks: the Fault-Gates, old forge-districts built over warm fissures
the Council Hall on its river bluff
the Nightmarket, where the Unmarked trade unregistered goods

regions.name: The Sunken Vale
regions.description: Once fertile lowlands, half-drowned decades ago by a Veil-storm that never fully receded. Dangerous, resource-rich, and largely unclaimed by anyone willing to say so out loud.
borders: open water south, where charts simply stop
landmarks: the drowned town's Belltower, still rung by storms
the Reedroads, passable only by flatboat or by those who know the paths

regions.name: The Greywood
regions.description: An old, watchful forest that remembers more of the world's true age than anyone currently living does. Home to things that were never quite human to begin with, and were here long before Aetherfall had a name.
borders: the Hollow March west of the eaves
no mapped southern or eastern edge - travelers who push on report the forest simply continues
landmarks: the Nameless Door, a bare stone slab that predates the forest and matches no known Veil site
the Eaves-towns, where wood-folk trade with outsiders without quite inviting them in

history.name: The First Quiet
history.description: The world nobody remembers. The Greywood's eldest things predate every name, road, and ruin anyone still uses; whatever came before is legend even to legends.

history.name: When Thin Places Were Mapped
history.description: Scholars and mariners first documented the places where the Veil runs thin. Arrivals had been happening for generations before - folklore called the strangers ghosts, omens, returned dead - but this is when Aetherfall understood what it was looking at, and named the Veil.

history.name: The Founding of Emberreach
history.description: Built over the great warm fault where the Veil bleeds heat into stone, by arrivals and native folk together. It grew into the world's one true city: part harbor for the displaced, part market for wonder, part argument about all of it.

history.name: The Drowning of the Vale
history.description: A single Veil-storm drowned the fertile lowlands overnight and never fully receded - standing proof that the Veil is not merely a door but weather, and that it does not care what stands in the way. The Remnant have lived on the flood's edge ever since.

history.name: The Long Watch
history.description: Arrivals have grown rarer these last years. No one will say plainly whether that means the Veil is healing or closing - least of all Ashwren, who keeps count better than anyone alive.

factions.name: The Wardens of the Veil
factions.kind: keeper-of-crossings order, currently one person strong
factions.description: Ashwren's office, such as it is: keep watch at arrival sites, greet the arrived, keep the count, and know the way home. Most of Aetherfall believes the Wardens died out generations ago; the ones who matter know otherwise.

factions.name: The Emberreach Council
factions.description: Pragmatic, tax-hungry, and genuinely useful. Registers Veil-Touched names in a great ledger (registration is voluntary; the Unmarked never do), keeps the dike against the Drowned Fields, and treats the Veil as infrastructure.

factions.name: The Unmarked
factions.description: Veil-Touched who never registered, living in every city's gaps under their own-world names. They remember each other's homes, keep each other fed, and trust institutions exactly as far as they must.

factions.name: The Cartographers' Guild
factions.kind: guild of mapmakers and thin-place surveyors
factions.description: Charts the Veil's behavior and sells passage-knowledge dearly. Half-convinced the Veil opens both ways on schedule somewhere, if only someone could read the pattern - an obsession that funds real science and real folly in equal measure.

factions.name: The Quiet Choir
factions.description: Teaches that going home costs exactly what you deserve to lose, no more and no less. Helps travelers reach crossings - sometimes honestly. Gentle-voiced, patient, and wrong in ways that are hard to argue with.

peoples.name: The Born
peoples.description: Native folk of Aetherfall. Most will never meet a Veil-Touched; to them arrivals are story-folk, half miracle and half bad omen, and both reactions look identical from outside.

peoples.name: The Veil-Touched
peoples.description: The arrived. They share nothing except the fact of arrival - different centuries, different worlds, nothing else - making them a diaspora whose only homeland is each other's company.

peoples.name: The Elderwood Folk
peoples.description: Never quite human; were here before names. Slow to speak, slower to lie, and quietly withdrawing deeper into the green as the world gets louder. Their friendships last longer than kingdoms; so do their grudges.

peoples.name: The Remnant
peoples.description: Descendants of the Sunken Vale, river-dwellers since the drowning. Flatboat-borne, close-mouthed about the safe paths, and the only people who treat the Drowned Fields as home instead of warning.

glossary.meaning: open syllables and soft endings - Ashwren, Halveth, Emberreach, Wrenlow. Avoid hard k/x/z sounds; they mark a name as foreign.
Torvin, Rowan, anything from home - unchanged, which is exactly how natives spot them. The foreignness is the identity.

glossary.term: Places are named for what happened there
glossary.meaning: never for owners or founders: the Hollow March marches hollowly, the Sunken Vale sank, Emberreach reached for embers. Follow this rule for new places.

glossary.term: Old things get plain compound names
glossary.meaning: Standing Stones, Nameless Door, Fault-Gates, Milestone Road - solid, functional, Anglo-saxon-flavored compounds.

glossary.term: New things get founder or trade names
glossary.meaning: the Council Hall, the Nightmarket, Reedroads - named by whoever built or used them, practically.

glossary.term: Faction titles are plain and slightly bureaucratic
glossary.meaning: Warden, Council, Guild, Choir - no grandiose self-styling except the cults, who do style themselves grandly.

geography_notes: The Hollow March sits at the world's northern edge, six days' south road from Emberreach - the only reliable route, walked by every arrival before you. The Elderwood borders the March eastward without a clear edge; the Drowned Fields lie west beyond Emberreach's dike, and south of them the maps stop pretending. Distances are measured in days on foot, rivers run toward Emberreach from everywhere, and nobody has ever charted the world's far side - the Veil-edge country wraps around the known lands like a shoreline with no ocean.
central_tension: The way home is not a secret - the Veil genuinely does open again, on its own uncertain rhythm, at sites Ashwren can name outright. But stepping through costs something real: a memory, a name, a piece of who you were before you arrived, chosen unknowing by the Veil itself, never by the one crossing it. Every Veil-Touched eventually has to decide, honestly, whether going home is worth what it takes - or whether Aetherfall has already become home enough to stay.

who_what_where_when_why.who: You were, until moments ago, living an entirely ordinary life - whatever it was that nearly ended it, an accident, an illness, a violence you didn't choose, doesn't matter anymore. Only that it nearly did.
who_what_where_when_why.what: The Veil between your world and this one happened to thin at exactly the moment your own life did, and it pulled you through rather than let you go.
who_what_where_when_why.where: This is Aetherfall - specifically, the Hollow March, where every Veil-Touched arrival is drawn first, without exception.
who_what_where_when_why.when: Aetherfall keeps its own time, entirely indifferent to your world's calendar. You may find only a day has passed back home when you return, or a lifetime - there is no way to know which until you actually do, if you ever do.
who_what_where_when_why.why: No one truly knows why the Veil chooses who it chooses. Ashwren has a theory - that it takes those whose story genuinely wasn't finished yet - but says plainly that it's only a theory, not a certainty, and has never claimed otherwise.

tone_guidance: Grounded and character-driven, not zany or played for comedy. Wonder and real danger in roughly equal measure. Aetherfall is strange, but never senseless - it has real rules, real history, real consequences - the tone of a world that takes itself seriously, even in a scene that's lighthearted in the moment. Old things should feel old, distances should cost what they cost, and the small choices of ordinary people should carry the weight of epics.
